events.text: I want to throw a surprise 50th birthday party for my wife
Finding the first contact a pro would call…
Hi, I'm Priya, an event planner. Surprise 50ths can look so many different ways, from an intimate dinner to a big bash. To steer this right, what kind of vibe are you picturing?
Backyard party with family
I want to throw a surprise 50th birthday party for my wife (backyard party with family)
Got it. For that I'm bringing in 5 Pros. Surprise logic locks first, then food and look, then entertainment pacing, and finally how we capture the reveal.
Hi, I'm Dev, your surprise logistics coordinator. Owns the decoy plan, arrival timing, and guest wrangling.
Hi, I'm Marco, your private chef & caterer. Owns menu design, dietary needs, and food service flow.
Hi, I'm Juno, your event designer & florist. Owns look, feel, florals, and tablescape.
Hi, I'm Theo, your entertainment & av lead. Owns music, sound, speeches, and pacing.
Hi, I'm Ines, your event photographer. Owns the reveal shot and memory capture.
Juno is building the reveal around her aesthetic. Who's getting her to the surprise location?
A close friend
Roughly how many guests are you picturing?
Any dietary restrictions among the guest list?
Vegetarian, Gluten-free
What food style fits her vibe best?
Buffet stations
Which aesthetic feels most like her?
Nostalgic throwback
Juno's aesthetic is set. What should the music do?
Dance floor energy
Dev's wrangling about 20–40 guests in. What matters most to capture?
The reveal reaction
That's everything we need up front. Give us a moment while your Staff writes up your plan.
Your Staff is writing your plan…
Your plan is ready.

logistics: Brief the close friend with a decoy story like a dinner date; have her arrive 30 minutes after guests to allow setup buffer.
Set a guest arrival window 45–60 minutes before reveal; collect phones or ask for a social media blackout until after the surprise.
Park guest cars around the block or at a neighbor's to keep the driveway clean of spoilers.
Build a plan B indoor pivot if weather turns; confirm forecast 72 hours out.
caterer: Plan 6–8 buffet items with clear vegetarian and gluten-free labels; aim for 1.5 lbs food per guest across stations.
Collect final RSVPs with allergy confirmations 10 days out; keep two sealed allergy-safe plates aside in case of surprises.
Choose dishes that hold 30–45 minutes at temp in case her arrival slips; skip delicate fried items.
stylist: Lean into nostalgic throwback: decade she turned 20, framed photos, vinyl covers, and warm string lights for backyard dusk.
Skip lilies, hyacinth, and heavy jasmine near food; use low non-fragrant arrangements under 12 inches so sightlines stay open.
Keep signage warm, not roast-style; avoid 'Over the Hill' gags that could embarrass her in front of family.
entertainment: Book a DJ or build a 4-hour playlist weighted to her era; confirm her top 10 songs with the close friend quietly.
Rent a wireless handheld mic plus a small powered speaker for toasts, separate from the dance system, so the emotional peak lands.
Set dance floor after cake; keep volume under 85 dB during dinner so conversation works.
photographer: Pre-scout the reveal spot and mark two shooting positions covering her face and the crowd; have guests face the entry path.
Bring an on-camera flash with diffuser and a fast 35mm or 50mm lens for low light after sunset.
Shoot the first 15 minutes of reveal and hugs before any posed group photos.

steps: Priya locks the date, backyard layout, and final guest count by November 14 and sends save-the-dates with a secrecy note.
Dev briefs the close friend on the decoy story and arrival timing, and sets the guest arrival window 45 minutes early.
Marco finalizes the buffet menu with vegetarian and gluten-free labeled stations once RSVPs and allergies are in by three weeks out.
Juno orders nostalgic throwback decor, non-fragrant low florals, and string lights two weeks before the party.
Theo confirms the playlist with the close friend, rents the mic and speakers, and tests AV the morning of.
Ines scouts the reveal sightlines the day before and preps low-light gear for the dusk timeline.
